value:
Forward-looking effort estimates for the two Bun migrations, sized 2026-05-06. Binary-build swap and test-runner swap are independent decisions with very different cost shapes.

BINARY BUILD: SEA-Node → `bun build --compile` (HALF-DAY, v1.0.0-beta.2 scope)
- Replaces ~140-line scripts/sea-build.js (esbuild bundle → SEA blob → copy Node binary → postject inject → codesign) with ~20-30 line bun command. Drops esbuild + postject from devDependencies.
- CI matrix shape unchanged. macOS job simplifies: drop the Node x64 tarball download (bun cross-compiles via `--target=bun-darwin-x64` from arm64 runner). Keep `lipo -create` + `codesign --sign -` for universal binary — OS-level, not toolchain-bound.
- BLOCKER: src/storage.ts has `export { Scope }` where Scope is a type-only re-export. Bun's TS executor errors on this. One-line fix to `export type { Scope }`. Already documented in project.bunValidate issue #3.
- VALIDATION GAP: project.bunValidate confirmed `bun dist/mcp-server.js` (Bun runtime executing pre-compiled JS) byte-identical to Node. Did NOT test `bun build --compile` output (which embeds Bun runtime into a single executable — structurally different). One debug-tag rerun (v0.0.0-debug.0 pattern from #96) needed before committing.

TEST RUNNER: vitest → bun:test (2-4 FOCUSED DAYS, DEFER TO v1.1+)
- 59 test files in src/__tests__/, ~17.3K LOC, `globals: true` (no test file currently imports vitest)
- vitest API call counts: 396 vi.fn, 95 vi.mock across 31 files, 31 vi.resetModules, 29 vi.spyOn, 19 vi.mocked, 14 vi.clearAllMocks, 6 vi.doMock, 5 vi.importActual, 3 vi.hoisted
- DOMINANT COST is `vi.mock` hoisting (31 files): vitest's compiler transform auto-hoists vi.mock calls above all imports. bun:test's mock.module() runs in source order and does NOT auto-hoist. Since ESM `import` is itself hoisted by TS, you can't put a runtime mock.module() call "before" imports syntactically. Each of those 31 files needs per-file judgment: convert top-level imports of mocked modules to lazy `await import(...)` inside test setup, OR restructure so the mocked module is only referenced inside test bodies after mock.module() runs. Not a codemod.
- Other costs: mechanical renames (vi.fn → mock, vi.spyOn → spyOn) ~2-3 hr; rewrite vi.resetModules/vi.importActual patterns 2-4 hr; fix 2 entries-advanced.test.ts responseSize byte-counting failures (Bun's stdout capture differs from Node's) 0.5-2 hr; validate the 160 previously-skipped tests (zod transformer issue from validate session) load under native bun:test 1-3 hr; matcher edge-case drift 2-4 hr; coverage/CI/docs 1 hr.

GREENFIELD REWRITE EVALUATED, REJECTED:
The 1394 test cases encode a year of regression-guard sediment — each one is a decision about what edge case matters, what bug to prevent re-occurring. "Rewrite from scratch and decide what to test fresh" loses that. "Re-implement same coverage in new framework" is migration-cost + writing-cost (strictly more work). The only valid hybrid: per-file selective rewrites of mock-heavy files where the existing structure is gnarlier than just rewriting from understanding. Not a viable replacement for migration overall.

WHY THIS DROVE OPTION A IN project.bunValidate:
The cost asymmetry — half-day for the binary swap, 2-4 days for test runner — combined with the fact that test-runner choice is developer-internal (users don't see it) is exactly why Option A (Node-test / Bun-production split) is recommended for v1.0.0. Ship the user-visible Bun benefits cheaply; defer the toolchain-internal swap until v1.1+ when there's bandwidth and a separate reason (e.g. test perf, dropping Node from dev requirements entirely).
